purpose: Every archived URL is accounted for. A candidate map is not a publication or redirect approval; keep original backup files immutable. Route changes belong to the final reviewed recovery manifest.

methodology.grouping: Read generator source declarations without executing generator code; match archived slug to the longest declared subject, and collapse the two daily-work audiences into one theme. Legacy ungenerated slugs retain individual families. Identical declared subjects across series join a family.
methodology.repetition: Read-only initial audit normalized whitespace/lowercase on blank-line paragraphs of >=25 words. 4,257 archive files have >=50% of counted paragraph words also present in >=10 archive files; 4,228 have >=75%. This measures exact reuse, not plagiarism, fact accuracy, or a Google threshold.
methodology.externalEvidence: No archived body contained an http:// or https:// URL at audit start; citations still need verification when added.
methodology.keywordEvidence: No current country-specific search volume, ranking or Search Console recovery evidence was available. Family priority is editorial relevance, not measured keyword popularity.

reviewRules: Do not bulk-restore source files whose frontmatter still says published.
Do not redirect all topic-angle variations to one broad article merely because keywords overlap.
Use a permanent redirect only when the replacement answers the useful original intent; never redirect irrelevant pages to the home page or a service page.
Preserve original publication date on a restored slug and record the actual substantial edit date.
No minimum word count is a Google requirement; require a complete useful answer rather than padding.
No fabricated results, local offices, market rates, rankings, keyword volumes, or competitor claims.
Current published 67 articles are retained. Source backup remains recoverable.
